name: Concatenating Strings and Numbers (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that uses variables x, y, and z to print "Python was invented in 1989.".
code:
#Step 1: Assign initial values to the variables x, y, and z
x = "Python was invented in "
y = 1989
z = "."
#Step 2: Print the text using the variables initialized above 
print(x + str(y) + z)

comments.content: This statement sets variable x to the string "Python was invented in ".
This statement sets variable y to the integer 1989.
This statement sets variable z to the string ".".

This statement concatenates the content of variables x, y, and z to print the requested output. We concatenate the content of these variables using the + operator. Variables x and z have a string value and we can use the + operator to concatenate their content. Variable y, on the other hand, has an integer value and its value can be concatenated with strings only when it is explicitly converted to a string using the str function.
Note that the concatenating and printing are done in the same line. That is, we don't have to store the concatenated string to a new variable at first and then print it in the next line.
Note that the + operator creates a new string from the contents of its operands joined. This string will be printed by the print function and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
